question: The mean, median, and unique mode of the positive integers \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) \(6,\) \(7,\) and \(x\) are all equal. What is the value of \(x?\)
solution:
The number \(6\) already occurs twice. Adding one value \(x\) can make another number occur at most twice, which would only tie \(6\). Therefore, if the mode is unique, it must be \(6\).

The mean must also be \(6\), so the seven numbers must total \(7\cdot6=42\). The six known numbers total \(31\), giving
\[
x=42-31=11.
\]
For this value, the ordered list is \(3,4,5,6,6,7,11\). Its fourth value, hence its median, is \(6\), and \(6\) is its unique mode. Thus all conditions hold, and \(\boxed{x=11}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
